findings.F1: Over the next 10 days, a coin's 10-day return scaled by its 20-day daily volatility predicts its excess return better than the range position does. Pooled, the slope is 0.094 of the coin's usual 10-day move per unit of z, with t 3.62 over 1403 non-overlapping cases. Fitted together with the 30-day range position and the 30-day z, the 10-day z keeps a coefficient of 0.155 (t 3.70), while the range position falls to −0.104 (t −1.27) and the 30-day z to 0.011 (t 0.27).
findings.F2: After a large one-day move in a high-volatility coin, the next day tends to go the other way. In the top third of each coin's 20-day volatility, the next-day excess return has a slope of −0.134 standard deviations per unit of the one-day z, with t −7.39 over 4830 days. The same slope is +0.020 (t 1.89) in the low-volatility third, and −0.038 (t −4.61) pooled over 14500 days.
findings.F3: The one-day reversal is strongest after the largest falls. The bottom fifth of one-day z is followed by +0.39 % next-day excess return (t 4.04, 2900 days), which is twice the 0.19 % cost of a trade. It is negative in all eight years, with t ≤ −3 in 2018, 2020 and 2023, and negative in all six coins, ranging from −0.006 for ZEC to −0.093 for XMR (t −4.67).
findings.F4: The 10-day continuation does not come from the last day. With the last day split out, the prior 9-day z has a coefficient of 0.088 (t 3.30) against 0.019 (t 0.76) for the last day's z. Measured from one day after the signal, the 9-day z still has 0.058 (t 2.17).
findings.F5: The 10-day continuation is uneven across years and coins, so it is not settled. Across years the slope ranges from −0.059 in 2022 to +0.266 (t 3.45) in 2020 and +0.151 (t 2.51) in 2024, and it is positive in all six coins (XRP 0.183, t 2.96; LTC 0.009). Across quintiles of the 10-day z, the next 10 days' excess return is −2.0 % in the second and third quintiles against +2.4 % (t 2.23) in the top quintile.
findings.F6: The brief's reversion does not show in flat coins. In the flat half of the 30-day trend measure, the next 10 days' excess return is −0.39 % (t −0.39) at the bottom third of the range and +0.11 % (t 0.09) at the top third. The tested continuation also shows only in trending coins: +1.33 % (t 1.16) at the top third.
findings.F7: The book's gain sits in a few large days, and the longs carry it.
findings.F8: There is a weekday pattern in the next-day excess return, but it is not stable enough to act on. Next-day excess return after Thursday and Friday closes exceeds that after Monday and Wednesday closes by 1.76 % in 2019 (t 7.0), 0.77 % in 2024 (t 3.05) and 0.51 % in 2025 (t 2.0), but it turns negative in 2022 (−0.42 %, t −1.57). No idea is drawn from it, because a weekday is not a graded situation.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 10-day return relative to its own recent daily volatility, the more the coin rises over the following 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A coin that has risen strongly over 10 days for its volatility is a reason to be long for the next 10 days, and one that has fallen strongly is a reason not to buy it.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled ten-day momentum

ideas.idea: When a coin's past 20 days have been highly volatile, the larger its one-day move relative to that volatility, the more the coin moves back the other way over the next day.
ideas.consequence: In a volatile coin, a sharp one-day fall is a reason to buy for the following day, and a sharp one-day rise is a reason not to chase it.
ideas.name: high-volatility one-day reversal
